title: Tamsin and the Postcard
premise: Quentin Yarrow, a ghostwriter who has built a career on other people's confessions, is hired to write the memoirs of Aldous Vane, a celebrated novelist whose early work she secretly loves. While sorting his archives on the Cornish island of Merrow's Reach, she finds an unsent postcard from eleven years ago, addressed to a woman named Tamsin, confessing a love he abandoned for ambition. When Quentin tracks down Tamsin, now running the island's last guesthouse, she discovers the postcard was never lost but hidden — and that her own arrival was arranged by Aldous to finally deliver it through someone else. As Quentin and Tamsin fall for each other, Quentin must choose between finishing the memoir as commissioned, exposing Aldous's curated lies, or burning the manuscript and writing the truth instead. The book ends with Quentin publishing the unvarnished story under her own name, staying on the island past the last ferry, and choosing a whole heart over a containable one.
about_author: Emrys Villalobos is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before writing fiction of their own. They live between coastal towns and write about the things we post, hide, and never send.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Quentin Yarrow's POV. In London, Quentin accepts a lucrative commission to ghostwrite Aldous Vane's memoirs, telling herself the heart is trainable and containable. A brief flashback shows her leaving a lover who wanted more than she'd give. Emotional beat: guarded competence masking old wounds.

chapters.title: Merrow's Reach
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She arrives by ferry at the tidal island where Aldous winters, meeting his brittle charm and his assistant's warnings about what stays in the archive. The guesthouse is run by a quiet woman named Tamsin, who doesn't read novels. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional excitement.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sorting decades of drafts and correspondence, Quentin notes gaps — years missing, letters removed. Aldous dictates polished half-truths while she transcribes. Tamsin delivers tea and lingers, asking sharp questions about what biography owes the living. Emotional beat: first crack in Quentin's neutrality.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Behind a false drawer back, Quentin finds an unsent postcard in Aldous's hand, addressed to 'Tamsin' at the guesthouse, confessing love and cowardice. She pockets it, telling herself it's research. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery tangled with guilt.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Doesn't Read
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin notices the new ghostwriter watching her too carefully. We learn her history: she came to the island years ago waiting for something that never arrived, and made peace with it. She likes Quentin's directness. Emotional beat: wary warmth, the ache of long patience.

chapters.title: What the Memoir Omits
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Aldous instructs her to cut a whole summer from the narrative — the same summer the postcard dates from. Quentin confronts him obliquely; he deflects with a story about protecting someone. She begins drafting two versions of every chapter. Emotional beat: loyalty to craft versus loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Storm Lanterns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A storm strands Quentin at the guesthouse overnight; they cook together, trade stories that aren't quite confessions. Tamsin almost mentions a letter she once expected, then doesn't. Emotional beat: intimacy arriving sideways, both women holding back their central secrets.

chapters.title: The Ferry Timetable
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin learns the ferry season ends in six weeks — after which the island is cut off until spring. The deadline reframes everything: finish the memoir, deliver the postcard, leave, or stay. Aldous grows suspicious of her questions. Emotional beat: time becoming a character.

chapters.title: Aldous Explains Himself
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV (first use). He admits he wrote the postcard the night before his breakthrough novel sold, and chose the book over the woman, believing love would keep. He hired Quentin partly because her name appeared in a letter Tamsin once wrote to a literary journal — he wanted the postcard delivered by someone Tamsin might trust. Emotional beat: vanity curdling into genuine remorse.

chapters.title: Pieces on Loan
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin and Quentin grow closer; Tamsin recognizes in herself the habit of lending pieces of her heart while keeping the whole safe. She lets Quentin see the room she keeps ready for a life that never started. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by the fear of being someone's second choice.

chapters.title: The Draft with Two Endings
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin finishes the sanitized memoir Aldous wants and secretly drafts the true one. Tamsin finds the true draft open on the table and reads her own name in it. She feels betrayed twice — by Aldous's silence and by Quentin's concealment. Emotional beat: the discovery scene, trust fracturing.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin tells Quentin the full story: how she waited, how she stopped waiting, how she rebuilt. She asks Quentin whether she was sent as a messenger or a substitute. Quentin can't honestly answer. Emotional beat: grief spoken plainly; the relationship suspended.

chapters.title: The Ghostwriter's Confession
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin realizes she has spent her career lending pieces — words, empathy, presence — while keeping her own name off everything. She confronts Aldous: she will not deliver his postcard like a courier; if truth gets told, it will be told properly. Emotional beat: reclaiming authorship of her own life.

chapters.title: What Aldous Never Sent
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Aldous, facing the memoir's publication and his own mortality (a diagnosis he's hidden), writes a second letter — this one honest about the cost of his choice, not just the feeling. He gives it to Quentin unsealed, surrendering control. Emotional beat: humility arriving too late to be convenient.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. With the causeway exposed, Tamsin walks the flats alone and decides she will not be a plot point in anyone's redemption. She packs, intending to take the last ferry out herself. Emotional beat: self-possession hard-won; the risk of losing love to preserve dignity.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On the final sailing day, Quentin must choose: board with the finished memoir and her old contained life, or stay with no contract, no byline plan, and a woman who may not forgive her. She hands Tamsin both letters — Aldous's and her own unfinished one. Emotional beat: the climax of choice.

chapters.title: Both Letters
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin reads Aldous's letter and feels the eleven-year wound close — not healed, but closed. Then she reads Quentin's, which asks nothing and offers everything: no messenger, no substitute, just a woman who stayed past the last ferry. Emotional beat: grief and hope reconciling.

chapters.title: Burning the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin burns Aldous's sanitized memoir in the archive grate and tells him she'll publish the true version under her own name, with his consent or without his blessing. Aldous, unexpectedly, signs the release — his last act of courage. Emotional beat: destruction as honesty; the ghostwriter becomes an author.

chapters.title: Wintering
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The island closes for winter; the two women learn each other without deadlines or departures. Small scenes: mending the guesthouse roof, arguing about endings, Tamsin teaching Quentin to stay when conversation gets hard. Emotional beat: love as daily practice, not declaration.

chapters.title: The Book Called Tamsin
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The true memoir publishes under Quentin's name, titled simply 'Tamsin,' with Aldous's cooperation and Tamsin's approval of every page about her. Reviews call it his best work and her debut at once. Emotional beat: vindication tempered by the knowledge that some truths cost what they're worth.

chapters.title: First Ferry of Spring
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Spring returns; the first ferry brings guests, letters, and Aldous himself, frail, come to apologize in person. Tamsin lets him sit in the garden but not inside. Forgiveness given in exact measure. Emotional beat: closure without absolution.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, closing on both. One year on: Quentin writes her own second book; Tamsin repaints the guesthouse sign to read 'Tamsin & Co.' A new postcard arrives — this one sent, signed by both, mailed to no one in particular, kept on the mantel. Emotional beat: the heart, uncontained, thriving anyway.
